title: Help Center navigation proposal: troubleshooting + known issues hub (IA, labels, cross-links)
content:
Context
- Support + CS are running a “known-issues sprint” to publish copy/paste-ready workarounds and link them consistently from Support workflows.
- DevEx/Docs needs to make this content discoverable for customers and Support, without burying it under product docs or creating a parallel “support wiki”.
- Current state: troubleshooting guidance is scattered across SDK guides, API references, and a few ad-hoc pages. Known issues exist (or are being drafted) but aren’t consistently reachable from:
  - docs site global nav
  - SDK “Getting Started” and “Streaming” pages
  - API error code pages
  - Console UI help links

Problem statement
Customers are failing to find the “right” mitigation fast enough.
- Repeat tickets for the same symptoms (stream disconnects, 429 confusion, audit log lag) even when there is a known workaround.
- Support spends time pasting the same diagnostic steps / retry guidance.
- When customers do find a page, they often land on a deep link without context (“is this current?”, “does it apply to my tier/region?”, “when do I escalate?”).

Goals
1) Make troubleshooting + known issues content easy to discover within 1–2 clicks from:
   - docs home
   - SDK guides (Python/TS/Go)
   - API reference error sections
2) Standardize labels and page layout so customers can quickly answer:
   - Is this affecting Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
   - Which regions/models?
   - What’s the workaround?
   - When should I escalate / open a ticket?
3) Reduce repeat tickets and shorten time-to-mitigation by improving self-serve discovery.
4) Ensure content fits incident comms guidance (status page vs docs banner vs KB update) and does not leak customer-specific details.

Non-goals
- Rewriting the full docs IA or product taxonomy.
- Building an entirely new “support portal” separate from docs.
- Publishing sensitive incident timelines or customer-identifying details.

Audience
- Primary: developers integrating Redwood API + SDKs (Hosted) and operators/platform engineers running Dedicated/Private.
- Secondary: Support/CS (needs consistent links and anchor targets for macros; uses pages during live escalations).

Proposal summary (recommended IA)
Add a top-level “Help Center” (or “Support”) entry in docs navigation with two major hubs:
A) Troubleshooting Hub (symptom-driven, “how to debug”)
B) Known Issues & Workarounds Hub (issue-driven, “temporary mitigations + escalation criteria”)

Recommended top-nav label
Option 1: “Help Center” (customer-friendly, avoids implying paid-only support)
Option 2: “Troubleshooting” (direct but may under-scope known issues)
Recommendation: “Help Center” with landing page that immediately splits into Troubleshooting vs Known Issues.

Information Architecture (draft)
1) Help Center (landing)
   - “Start here: diagnose common failures” (Troubleshooting)
   - “Known issues & workarounds” (Known Issues)
   - “Contact Support” (gated content/CTA; tier-aware messaging)
   - “Status / incidents” (link to status page; brief explanation of how we communicate)

2) Troubleshooting Hub (symptoms)
   Organize by customer-observable symptoms, not internal components.
   - API requests failing
     - 401/403 auth errors
     - 404/410 model not found / deprecated
     - 429 rate limits & quotas
     - 5xx server errors
   - Latency & timeouts
     - High latency (p50 vs p99)
     - Request timeouts
     - Region-specific degradation
   - Streaming
     - Stream disconnects / connection resets
     - Truncated streams
     - Reconnect + idempotency
   - Webhooks & callbacks
     - TLS/cert validation
     - Retries and signature verification
   - Dedicated
     - Throughput drops
     - Autoscaling behavior
   - Private / VPC
     - Installer/upgrade failures
     - DNS/network connectivity
     - Audit logs + compliance artifacts

   Each troubleshooting page should follow a consistent format:
   - What you’ll see (symptoms)
   - Quick checks (2–5 steps)
   - Common causes (by likelihood)
   - Mitigations you can try now
   - What to collect for Support (request IDs, region, model, SDK version)
   - Links: related known issues / status guidance

3) Known Issues & Workarounds Hub (issue-driven)
   Landing page provides:
   - filter/tag chips (Tier, Region, Product area, Model family)
   - “Last updated” prominence (recency is critical for trust)
   - clear “When to escalate” callout on each card

   Proposed tags (keep constrained; avoid tag explosion)
   - Tier: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
   - Product: API Gateway | Runtime/Serving | Console | Routing/Fallback | Billing/Metering | Auth/SSO | Audit Logs | Private Installer
   - Region: us-east | us-west | eu-west | ap-southeast (use canonical region strings from console)
   - Model family: (only if it materially changes workaround) e.g., “Llama-3.x”, “Mixtral”, “Embedding models”, “Rerank models”

   Known issue article template (required sections)
   - Summary (1–2 sentences)
   - Symptoms
   - Impact / blast radius
   - Who is affected (tier/regions/models)
   - Workaround / mitigation (copy/paste; safe defaults)
   - Validation: how to confirm improvement
   - When to escalate (explicit triggers + what to include)
   - Status / next steps (if there is an engineering ticket or target fix window)
   - Last updated + owner

Cross-linking strategy (where customers actually land)
1) SDK docs
- Add “Troubleshooting” sections to SDK guides for high-volume issues.
- Streaming pages should link to:
  - Streaming troubleshooting page
  - Known issue: “Streaming timeouts & reconnect”
- Rate limiting sections should link to:
  - 429 troubleshooting page
  - Known issue: “Quota mismatch and rate limit headers” (while ENG-4825 rolls out)

2) API reference
- On error response docs, add short “If you’re seeing this in production…” blocks with links to the matching troubleshooting page.
- For 429: link to a single canonical explanation page (avoid multiple competing pages).

3) Console
- Where possible, add “Need help?” links that go to the troubleshooting hub with preselected filter (if we can pass query params) or at least a stable anchor.

4) Support macros
- Ensure Support macros point to stable canonical pages (avoid deep links that will churn).
- Where a workaround is temporary or in flux, macros should link to the known issue page (which can be updated), not a one-off Slack snippet.

Navigation details (site UI)
- Add a persistent top-nav item: Help Center
- Add left-nav grouping within Help Center:
  - Troubleshooting
  - Known issues & workarounds
  - Contact Support
  - Status & incident communications

Naming conventions
- Use “Known issues” (plural) consistently across nav and page titles.
- Use “Workaround” in article titles where applicable.
  Examples:
  - “Workaround: Streaming timeouts and reconnect”
  - “Workaround: 429 quota mismatch and rate-limit headers”
  - “Workaround: Dedicated autoscaling oscillation”
  - “Workaround: Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations”

Content governance
Owners
- Known issue pages: Support/CS owns initial drafting; Eng/SRE must validate workaround; Docs owns publishing quality + consistency.
- Troubleshooting pages: Docs/DevEx owns, with Eng/SRE review on diagnostics accuracy.

Update cadence
- Known issues landing shows “Last updated”. If a known issue is not updated within N days (suggest: 30), add an internal review reminder (Docs automation or backlog ticket).

Sensitivity / policy
- No customer-identifying details.
- Avoid publishing root cause details that are speculative or security-sensitive; stick to symptoms + mitigations.
- Align with incident comms guidance: status page is the canonical source for ongoing incidents; docs pages provide evergreen mitigations and escalation criteria.

Metrics (success criteria)
Primary
- Ticket deflection for top known issues (Support to track in Jira via macro usage + linked article views).
- Reduction in time-to-first-mitigation for escalations where a workaround exists.
Secondary
- Docs analytics: % of sessions reaching Help Center, CTR from SDK pages to troubleshooting, and bounce rate.
- Search success: top queries leading to Help Center pages.

Implementation plan (phased)
Phase 0 (this sprint, aligned to known-issues sprint)
- Publish Help Center landing page and Known Issues landing page with initial set of articles.
- Add cross-links from:
  - SDK streaming troubleshooting
  - 429/rate limit docs
- Ensure each known issue article includes “When to escalate” and “What to collect for Support”.

Phase 1 (next 1–2 weeks)
- Add symptom-driven troubleshooting pages for:
  - 429s
  - streaming disconnects
  - audit log delivery latency
  - Dedicated autoscaling/latency
  - Private upgrade failures
- Add minimal nav refinements and “Related pages” blocks.

Phase 2 (cleanup + adoption)
- Add tagging/filter UX improvements per DES-233.
- Add docs banners guidance per DES-234 and make sure teams know when to use them.
- Work with Support ops to update macros library to canonical links.

Open questions
1) What is the right public label: “Help Center” vs “Support”?
   - Support may imply paid-only support; Help Center is neutral.
2) How do we handle tier-aware “Contact Support” messaging on docs?
   - Suggest: page describes how to open a ticket, but avoids exposing internal SLAs; link to customer portal auth for enterprise.
3) Should “Known issues” be indexed by symptom or by component?
   - Proposal: keep known issues issue-driven with tags; troubleshooting is symptom-driven.
4) Who is the DRI for “Last updated” freshness when the underlying engineering work changes status?
   - Proposal: Support ops (Dev Patel) owns weekly review; Docs enforces template and reminders.

Dependencies / related work
- ENG-4826: implement known-issues landing, tagging, and cross-links.
- DES-233: landing layout for known issues.
- DES-234: banner vs status page guidelines.
- ENG-4827: SDK streaming troubleshooting language alignment.

Appendix: proposed initial landing copy (draft)
Help Center
Find answers fast—troubleshoot common integration issues, review current known issues and workarounds, and learn when to contact Support.

Buttons
- Troubleshooting (diagnose by symptom)
- Known issues & workarounds (temporary mitigations + escalation criteria)

Footer note
For active incidents, our status page is the source of truth. Workaround articles are updated as we validate mitigations.
